Card.Occupants: ___E:President of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ and the ___E:First Family U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Family_of_the_United_States)___

Main.sentence: Camp David is a 125-acre (51-hectare) country retreat for the ___E:president of the United States U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States)___ .

It lies in the wooded hills of ___E:Catoctin Mountain Park U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catoctin_Mountain_Park)___ , in ___E:Frederick County, Maryland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_County,_Maryland)___ , near the towns of ___E:Thurmont U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thurmont,_Maryland)___ and ___E:Emmitsburg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emmitsburg,_Maryland)___ , about 62 miles (100 kilometers) north-northwest of the national capital city, ___E:Washington, D.C. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C.)___    It is code-named Naval Support Facility Thurmont .

Technically a military installation, it is staffed primarily by the ___E:Seabees U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seabees)___ , the ___E:Civil Engineer Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_Engineer_Corps)___ (CEC), the ___E:United States Navy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Navy)___ , and the ___E:United States Marine Corps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Marine_Corps)___ .
Naval construction battalions are tasked with Camp David construction and send detachments as needed.

Originally known as Hi-Catoctin , Camp David was built as a retreat for federal government agents and their families by the ___E:Works Progress Administration U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Works_Progress_Administration)___ .

Construction started in 1935 and was completed in 1938.  In 1942, President ___E:Franklin D. Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt)___ converted it to a presidential retreat and renamed it " Shangri-La ", after the ___E:fictional Himalayan paradise U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shangri-La)___ .

Camp David received its present name in 1953 from President ___E:Dwight D. Eisenhower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_D._Eisenhower)___ , in honor of his father and his ___E:grandson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Eisenhower)___ , both named David.

The Catoctin Mountain Park does not indicate the location of Camp David on park maps due to privacy and security concerns,  although it can be seen through the use of publicly accessible satellite images, and is also viewable on certain public web mapping services like ___E:Google Maps U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Google_Maps)___ .

Camp David has been used to host private ___E:diplomatic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplomacy)___ meetings with foreign leaders and ___E:heads of state U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_state)___ since at least ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ . ___E:Franklin D. Roosevelt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_D._Roosevelt)___ hosted ___E:Winston Churchill U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill)___ at Shangri-La in May 1943, during ___E:World War II U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II)___ .  ___E:Dwight Eisenhower U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwight_Eisenhower)___ held his first post heart-attack cabinet meeting there on November 22, 1955, following hospitalization and convalescence he required after a heart attack suffered in ___E:Denver, Colorado U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denver)___ , on September 24.  Eisenhower met ___E:Nikita Khrushchev U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikita_Khrushchev)___ there for two days of discussions in September 1959.

___E:John F. Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy)___ and his family often enjoyed riding and other recreational activities there, and Kennedy often allowed ___E:White House U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House)___ staff and Cabinet members to use the retreat when he or his family were not there.  ___E:Lyndon B. Johnson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson)___ met with advisors in this setting and hosted both ___E:Australian prime minister U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Australia)___ ___E:Harold Holt U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harold_Holt)___ and ___E:Canadian prime minister U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Canada)___ ___E:Lester B. Pearson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lester_B._Pearson)___ there.  ___E:Richard Nixon U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Nixon)___ was a frequent visitor.

He personally directed the construction of a swimming pool and other improvements to Aspen Lodge.  ___E:Gerald Ford U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford)___ hosted ___E:Indonesian president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Indonesia)___ ___E:Suharto U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suharto)___ at Camp David.

___E:Jimmy Carter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Carter)___ initially favored closing Camp David in order to save money, but once he visited the retreat, he decided to keep it.  Carter brokered the ___E:Camp David Accords U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_David_Accords)___ there in September 1978 between ___E:Egyptian president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Egypt)___ ___E:Anwar al-Sadat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anwar_Sadat)___ and ___E:Israeli prime minister U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Israel)___ ___E:Menachem Begin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Menachem_Begin)___ .  ___E:Ronald Reagan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan)___ visited the retreat more than any other president.

In 1984, Reagan hosted ___E:British prime minister U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_the_United_Kingdom)___ ___E:Margaret Thatcher U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Thatcher)___ .

Reagan restored the nature trails that Nixon paved over so he could horseback ride at Camp David.  ___E:George H. W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush)___ 's daughter, ___E:Dorothy Bush Koch U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Bush_Koch)___ , was married there in 1992, in the first wedding held at Camp David.
During his tenure as president, ___E:Bill Clinton U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton)___ spent every Thanksgiving at Camp David with his family.

In July 2000, he hosted the ___E:2000 Camp David Summit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Camp_David_Summit)___ negotiations between Israeli prime minister ___E:Ehud Barak U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ehud_Barak)___ and Palestinian Authority chairman ___E:Yasser Arafat U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasser_Arafat)___ there.

In February 2001, ___E:George W. Bush U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush)___ held his first meeting with a European leader, British prime minister ___E:Tony Blair U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Blair)___ , at Camp David, to discuss missile defense, Iraq, and NATO.  After the ___E:September 11 attacks U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/September_11_attacks)___ , Bush held a Cabinet meeting at Camp David to prepare the ___E:United States invasion of Afghanistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_invasion_of_Afghanistan)___ .
During his two terms in office, Bush visited Camp David 149 times, for a total of 487 days, for hosting foreign visitors as well as a personal retreat.
He met Blair there four times.

Among the numerous other foreign leaders he hosted at Camp David  were ___E:Russian president U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_Russia)___ ___E:Vladimir Putin U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vladimir_Putin)___   and President ___E:Musharraf U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musharraf)___ of ___E:Pakistan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan)___ in 2003,  ___E:Danish prime minister U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Denmark)___ ___E:Anders Fogh Rasmussen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anders_Fogh_Rasmussen)___ in June 2006,  and British prime minister ___E:Gordon Brown U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Brown)___ in 2007.

___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ chose Camp David to host the ___E:38th G8 summit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/38th_G8_summit)___ in 2012.  President Obama also hosted ___E:Russian prime minister U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Russia)___ ___E:Dmitry Medvedev U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dmitry_Medvedev)___ at Camp David,  as well as the ___E:GCC U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_Cooperation_Council)___ Summit there in 2015.

___E:Donald Trump U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump)___ hosted Senate majority leader ___E:Mitch McConnell U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitch_McConnell)___ and Speaker of the House ___E:Paul Ryan U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Ryan)___ at Camp David while the ___E:Republican Party U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States))___ prepared to defend both houses of Congress in the ___E:2018 midterm elections U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_midterm_elections)___ .

Trump also planned to meet with the ___E:Taliban U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taliban)___ at Camp David to negotiate ___E:a peace agreement U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States%E2%80%93Taliban_deal)___ in 2019, but refrained after ___E:a suicide bombing in Kabul U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/5_September_2019_Kabul_bombing)___ killed US troops.

The ___E:46th G7 summit U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/46th_G7_summit)___ was to be held at Camp David on June 10–12, 2020, but was cancelled due to health concerns during what was at the time considered the height of the ___E:COVID-19 pandemic U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic)___ .

___E:Joe Biden U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden)___ hosted the U.S.–Japan–Korea Summit with Japanese prime minister ___E:Fumio Kishida U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fumio_Kishida)___ and South Korean president ___E:Yoon Suk Yeol U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yoon_Suk_Yeol)___ at Camp David in August 2023, resulting in the declaration of the ___E:Camp David Principles U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_David_Principles)___ on trilateral relations between the U.S., Japan, and South Korea.

To be able to play his favorite sport, President Eisenhower had golf course architect ___E:Robert Trent Jones U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Trent_Jones)___ design a practice golf facility at Camp David.
Around 1954, Jones built one golf hole—a par 3—with four different tees; Eisenhower added a 250-yard (230 m) driving range near the helicopter landing zone.

On July 2, 2011, an ___E:F-15 U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McDonnell_Douglas_F-15_Eagle)___ intercepted a civilian aircraft approximately 6 miles (10 km) from Camp David, when ___E:President Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ was in the residence.
The two-seater, which was out of radio communication, was escorted to nearby ___E:Hagerstown, Maryland U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hagerstown,_Maryland)___ , without incident.
On July 10, 2011, an F-15 intercepted another small plane near Camp David when Obama was again in the residence; a total of three were intercepted that weekend.
